jobs.title: Bilingual Writers' Room Intern at 826 Boston
jobs.description: Employer: 826 Boston Expires: 10/29/2026 If you choose to apply for an 826 Boston internship, please complete the 826 Boston Internship Application and upload your resume and a writing sample. Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be reviewed. About the OpportunityMargarita Muñiz Academy (Muñiz) opened in 2012 as the district’s first bilingual high school, offering classes in both English and Spanish. It is the site of 826 Boston’s fifth Writers’ Room, opening in 2024. The English/Spanish Muñiz Bilingual Writers’ Room Intern will work alongside our Muñiz Writers’ Room Manager, where they will become an integral part of students’ writing journeys. 826 Boston runs Writers’ Rooms at the following Boston Public Schools:John D. O’Bryant School of Mathematics and Science, 55 Malcolm X Boulevard, RoxburyDr. Albert D. Holland High School of Technology, 60 Washington Street, DorchesterBoston International Newcomers Academy, 100 Maxwell Street, DorchesterNew Mission High School, 655 Metropolitan Ave, Hyde ParkBoston Teachers Union K-8 Pilot School, 25 Walk Hill Street, Jamaica PlainMargarita Muñiz Academy, 20 Child Street, Jamaica PlainThis is an opportunity to learn about the day-to-day operations of a non-profit, while working with English Language Learning (ELL) students, gaining experience on best practices to support youth, and building connections with 826 Boston staff, school communities, and students. In addition, interns will participate in specialized training sessions and conversations with the rest of their cohort each semester (i.e. a discussion on how to support neurodivergent learners, a workshop on self-publishing, etc.) Candidates do not need to currently be enrolled in an academic program, but they must be 18 or older to apply. The internship has a flexible commitment of 15–20 hours per week for about four months. Fall interns typically serve from September to December. Programming in the Muñiz Writers’ Room is in-person and runs from 8:00 AM-4:00 PM, Mondays-Thursdays. Interns who are not otherwise receiving financial compensation will receive a one-time stipend after completing their internship. The stipend amounts range from $580 to $1,000, depending on the amount of hours an intern works each week. Interns who receive a stipend will also be eligible for transportation reimbursement for up to $100 each semester. This position is also eligible for Federal Work-Study compensation through some schools. If you are eligible for Federal Work-Study, please let us know and we will try to work with your school to see if we are an eligible community partner. Mission:826 Boston is a nonprofit writing, tutoring, and publishing organization where students in grades K-12 and beyond can share their stories, amplify their voices, and develop as leaders in school and in life. What you’ll do:Serve as a writing tutor to students seeking support in Spanish and English with writing assignments in the Muñiz Writers’ Room through class visits, individual drop-ins, writing workshops, and publication projects.Ability to build genuine relationships with a diverse group of people and embrace values of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.Offer support to student publications, as needed. Assist Writers’ Room staff with projects as requested, which include, but are not limited to administering surveys to students, updating writing resource materials, or helping decorate and maintain our whimsical, imaginative space.Meet weekly with your supervisor to communicate project progress, receive individualized training on tasks, and seek counsel when help is needed to execute goals.Help support afterschool Debate Club meetingsParticipate in individualized tutoring with students. Update lesson plans tailored to different writing styles Organize program resources in Google Drive. Skills and experiences:826 Boston recognizes that impostor syndrome and the confidence gap might prevent some applicants from applying. Few candidates will have all of the relevant experience listed below, but 826 Boston is committed to assessing candidates with transferable skills and a willingness to be trained for this role.Spanish bilingual proficiency required. Enthusiastic belief in the mission of 826 Boston, passion for writing and interest in social-emotional learning of youth.Interest in teaching/tutoring writing to students grades K-12.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Strong organizational skills and the ability to multitask.Familiarity with the Boston Public Schools system preferred, but not required.The ability to take direction, seek counsel when needed, proactively identify needs and opportunities, and propose programmatic changes. Application Instructions: Please complete the 826 Boston Internship Application and upload your resume and a writing sample.Your writing sample should not exceed 500 words and can be any genre—a piece of fiction, an academic essay, a long-form poem, etc. You are welcome to submit a cover letter as your writing sample if you prefer. Please only submit what you feel comfortable sharing with a future supervisor. Applications will be reviewed by 826 Boston on a rolling basis. If you have questions or would like to check on the status of your application, please contact intern@826boston.org. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state and/or local law. About Us826 Boston is part of a national network of youth writing centers, co-founded by the award-winning author Dave Eggers and educator Nínive Calegari, that were named in GOOD Magazine’s “30 Places We Want to Work.” Since opening in 2007, 826 Boston has delivered its free youth writing and tutoring programs to more than 32,000 students and has been recognized by The Boston Globe as one of the best places in the city to volunteer. 826 Boston’s youth writers have published their work in The New York Times, The Boston Globe, and in numerous award-winning 826 Boston books, including A Place for Me in the World, which was hailed as a “triumph of middle school education” by The Boston Globe. In 2013, the 826 National network garnered the prestigious American Literacy Prize awarded by the Library of Congress. 826 Boston Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Statement At 826 Boston, we honor and actively work toward diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) across our organization. We are committed to centering the voices of the students who we serve, to creating inclusive spaces, and to incorporating feedback from our community into our decision-making processes. Our DEI lens is always evolving through the courageous conversations in which we participate and the relationships that we build through our work and service. We strengthen our cultural competency through experience, training, and feedback, which informs the development of all new organizational practices and goals and the evaluation of all existing procedures.826 Boston is dedicated to providing a platform for student advocacy through writing and publishing opportunities. In our work and mission, we are committed to dismantling white supremacy culture by recognizing that we are complicit in systems of racism and oppression. We will work to hold ourselves accountable in addressing these harmful structures and behaviors. Accommodations826 Boston provides reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities at every stage of the application process. Disclosing a disability or requesting a need for accommodations is a separate process from admissions and will have absolutely no bearing on a candidate’s application status. 826 Boston will make every effort to meet your request, but specific requests are not guaranteed. If you need to request an accommodation, please contact intern@826boston.org.

jobs.title: Behavioral Health Care Manager at Embolden Therapeutic Services
jobs.description: Employer: Embolden Therapeutic Services Expires: 10/29/2026 Pay: $48,000.00 - $53,000.00 per yearJob description:Behavioral Health Care Manager — Pediatric Collaborative Care ModelOverviewEmbolden Therapeutic Services is seeking a Behavioral Health Care Manager (BHCM) to join a pediatric primary care practice in Northborough, MA as part of an innovative Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) program integrating behavioral health into primary care.The BHCM will work closely with pediatricians, families, and a consulting psychiatrist to support children and adolescents experiencing mild to moderate behavioral health concerns, including ADHD, anxiety, depression, adjustment concerns, and behavioral challenges. This role provides brief, evidence-based behavioral health interventions, symptom monitoring, care coordination, and treatment planning within a structured, team-based model.The BHCM is a fully integrated member of the pediatric care team and plays a key role in helping patients and families access timely behavioral health support through the trusted relationship with their family pediatrician. This role includes regular support, including comprehensive training, continuing education and professional development, weekly psychiatric consultation case review, one-on-one weekly meetings, team meetings and pre-licensure supervision (all included and paid time), clear workflows, and collaboration with the pediatrician.About the RoleThe BHCM is responsible for supporting and coordinating the behavioral health care of an assigned pediatric caseload in collaboration with the patient’s pediatrician.This is a treat-to-target role focused on measurable improvement. The BHCM uses validated screening tools, tracks symptoms over time, provides brief interventions, supports medication management when relevant, and helps coordinate additional services when a higher level of care or longer-term therapy is needed.The BHCM will meet with patients and families both individually and together, as clinically appropriate. Interventions may include psychoeducation, behavioral activation, problem-solving strategies, motivational interviewing, parent guidance, executive functioning support, coping skills, and care coordination with schools or community resources when indicated.Key ResponsibilitiesThe Pediatric BHCM will:Provide brief, evidence-based behavioral health interventions for children and adolescents in support of their pediatrician.Conduct initial behavioral health assessments following referral from the pediatrician.Use validated screening and monitoring tools to assess symptoms, functional impairment, risk, and treatment progress.Support patients and families with focused interventions such as motivational interviewing, behavioral activation, problem-solving, parent coaching, and skills-based behavioral strategies.Coordinate closely with pediatricians and the primary care team to support integrated behavioral health treatment.Participate in weekly caseload review with the consulting psychiatrist, with attention to new patients, patients who are not improving as expected, and patients with diagnostic or treatment complexity.Communicate psychiatric consultation recommendations to the pediatrician and support follow-through as appropriate.Support medication management by monitoring adherence, side effects, treatment response, and family concerns, within the appropriate scope of the BHCM role.Maintain data entry into our registry to systematically track patient engagement, symptom scores, treatment response, follow-up needs, and care gaps.Re-engage patients and families who miss appointments or need additional outreach.Provide timely documentation in the electronic health record and registry consistent with CoCM billing and clinical requirements.Coordinate referrals to specialty mental health care, school-based supports, community resources, social services, or higher levels of care when clinically indicated.Assist with accurate time tracking, documentation, and workflow steps needed for monthly CoCM billing.Ideal CandidateThe ideal candidate is clinically grounded, organized, collaborative, and comfortable working with a fast-paced pediatric medical setting. This person enjoys working with children, adolescents, parents, and medical providers, and can balance warmth with structure.Strong candidates will have experience with pediatric behavioral health, telehealth brief interventions, care coordination, and documentation. They should be comfortable working as part of a team and able to communicate clearly with families, pediatricians, psychiatrists, schools, and outside providers.QualificationsRequired:Bilingual (Spanish and English) required.Minimum education requirement: Bachelor’s degree in psychology, social work, counseling, human services, nursing, public health, child development, or another related behavioral health field.Candidates may be currently enrolled in a relevant master’s degree program or actively pursuing clinical licensure in a behavioral health field. Strong applicants will have foundational clinical training, supervised experience, or coursework related to child/adolescent development, behavioral health assessment, evidence-based intervention, care coordination, or family systems.Experience working with children, adolescents, and families.Demonstrated ability to provide engaging, developmentally appropriate telehealth services to children, adolescents, and families, including creative use of virtual tools, caregiver involvement, visual supports, and structured activities.Knowledge of common pediatric behavioral health concerns, including anxiety, depression, ADHD, behavioral challenges, and adjustment-related concerns.Ability to provide brief, evidence-based interventions in a structured model of care.Strong communication, documentation, and organizational skills.Ability to collaborate effectively with pediatricians, psychiatric consultants, families, and other members of the care team.Comfort using electronic health records, spreadsheets, and technology-based workflows.Preferred:Experience in pediatric primary care, integrated care, school-based behavioral health, community mental health, or medical settings.Familiarity with Collaborative Care, integrated behavioral health, or measurement-based care.Experience with motivational interviewing, behavioral activation, problem-solving treatment, CBT-informed interventions, parent guidance, or brief pediatric interventions.Experience using technology to enhance engagement with children, adolescents and their families.Working knowledge of psychopharmacology for common pediatric behavioral health conditions, within the appropriate scope of practice.Work EnvironmentThis position is based in a pediatric primary care practice in Northborough, Massachusetts. This role is designed as a hybrid position. The BHCM will initially work remotely while the program evaluates patient, family, and practice needs for in-person behavioral health support. As the program grows, some on-site presence in the Northborough practice may be added based on clinical demand, workflow needs, and care team collaboration.Because much of the initial care will be delivered virtually, the ideal candidate should be comfortable engaging children, adolescents, and caregivers through telehealth and able to use creativity, structure, and developmentally appropriate strategies to make virtual sessions clinically meaningful and engaging.The role is full-time, Monday through Friday, with typical daytime hours. There may be flexibility for occasional early evening appointments based on patient need, BHCM availability, and program scheduling. The BHCM will have access to licensed clinical supervision and support during scheduled patient care hours.Compensation and BenefitsCompensation is competitive and commensurate with education, experience, clinical training, and overall role fit. The higher end of the salary range is intended for candidates who demonstrate strong alignment with the position’s clinical needs, including pediatric behavioral health experience, the ability to provide creative and engaging telehealth services to children, adolescents, and families, and Spanish-language fluency.About Embolden Therapeutic ServicesEmbolden Therapeutic Services partners with primary care practices to bring behavioral health support directly into medical settings through the Collaborative Care Model. Our work focuses on improving access, strengthening care coordination, supporting measurable clinical improvement, and helping primary care teams meet the behavioral health needs of their patients.We believe children, adolescents, and families should be able to access meaningful behavioral health support without long delays, fragmented referrals, or unnecessary barriers. Our team is building a model of care that is practical, evidence-based, and deeply collaborative.Learn more about us by going to www.emboldents.com.Benefits: 401(k)401(k) matchingPaid time offProfessional development assistance Application Question(s): What Electronic Medical Records (EMR) have you utilized?This role is brief, structured, team-based, and connected to pediatric primary care. Please share what you know about the collaborative care model (CoCM).This is a hybrid position and involves in person (2 days per week) and online connection with the child, parents, the PCP and others as needed. What experience do you have working with children and families? Include any details about working remotely with this population. Education: Bachelor's (Required) Language: Portuguese (Preferred)Spanish (Required) Ability to Commute: Northborough, MA 01532 (Required) Work Location: Hybrid remote in Northborough, MA 01532

jobs.description: Employer: New York Legal Assistance Group Expires: 10/29/2026 About NYLAG:Founded in 1990, NYLAG is a leading civil legal services organization combating economic, racial, and social injustice by advocating for people experiencing poverty or in crisis. Our services include comprehensive, free civil legal services, financial empowerment, impact litigation, policy advocacy, and community partnerships. NYLAG exists because wealth should not determine who has access to justice. We aim to disrupt systemic racism by serving individuals and families whose legal and financial crises are often rooted in racial inequality. NYLAG goes to where the need is, providing services in more than 150 community sites (e.g. courts, hospitals, libraries) and on our Mobile Legal Help Center. NYLAG’s staff of 410 impacted the lives of nearly 129,000 people last year.Job descriptionNYLAG’s Financial Empowerment and Advocacy Unit (FEAU), established in 2009, serves a diverse range of clients across New York City, providing financial counseling and advocacy to help individuals achieve stability and independence. FEAU provides services at NYLAG’s office and community-based intake sites throughout New York City, including via our work with the Office of Financial Empowerment, the Human Resources Administration, and private funders.Financial counselors counsel, coach, educate, and empower low to moderate income New Yorkers and their families. The financial counselor will provide one-on-one assistance to help clients access formal banking relationships, establish and rebuild credit, organize their finances through budgeting, managing and reducing their debt, establishing savings, securing benefits, and understanding taxes to meet their short- and long-term financial goals. Duties and ResponsibilitiesFacilitate in-person and virtual one-on-one financial counseling & coaching for New Yorkers with low-to-moderate income at a variety of community-based organizations and at partner sites.Implement retention and engagement strategies to encourage clients to achieve their financial goals and maintain ongoing engagement. Foster and maintain strong and collaborative relationships with staff members and external stakeholders to ensure program success.Work collaboratively with colleagues, supervisors, and other service providers to ensure high-quality services.Engage in outreach through workshops, presentations, and direct outreach to prospective clients in partnership and under direction of partner sites as needed.Expand access to financial counseling services through client-centered, community-responsive services in-person at partner sites across NYC.Ensure data is entered accurately and timely in NYLAG’s case management system and in partner’s system(s), if applicable.Ensure client files are saved securely and fully in our central shared file system.Participate in the unit’s advocacy work by collaborating on blog posts and other activities to highlight our efforts towards advancing racial equity in the financial counseling field.QualificationsNYLAG seeks a highly motivated financial counselor with a bachelor’s degree and a minimum of five (5) years of full-time work experience, with a preferred background in financial counseling/coaching. Experience and maturity in working with a diverse range of partners, funders, and clients. Energy and desire to travel across the NYC metro area in the field working directly with clients at partner sites most days per week. Demonstrated ability to manage a caseload, meet program deliverables, and maintain accurate documentation. Commitment to providing client-centered services with cultural humility and effectively supporting participants at partner sites throughout NYC. Demonstrated capacity to work independently and strong desire to develop their financial counseling & coaching skill set. This is a position that offers the opportunity to get additional in-house training and further grow your career.Due to current program needs, preference will be given to applicants who are fluent in Spanish, including the ability to read, write, and speak Spanish proficiently. Preference will be given to applicants who have taken the Personal and Consumer Finance course endorsed by the Office of Financial Empowerment. NYLAG’s Commitment to Diversity and InclusionNYLAG is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. People of color, women, people with disabilities, immigrants, veterans, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people, and those with lived experiences in the communities we serve are strongly encouraged to apply.Employment type:☒ Full-timeProfessional Level:☒ ProfessionalSalary Range: NYLAG is a unionized workplace, and salaries are set pursuant to a collective bargaining agreement. The current salary range for this position is between $73,718- $77,743. Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401k, life insurance, long term disability, commuter benefits, flexible spending accounts (FSA) for Medical and Dependent care.Application Instructions: Please save resume and cover letter in one pdf.NYLAG is committed to a hybrid work policy for staff whose work does not require their full-time presence in the office. However, please note that this role does require in-person days at various sites. This policy is subject to change.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) at Alpaca Health
jobs.description: Employer: Alpaca Health Expires: 10/29/2026 Alpaca HealthWork Location: In Person If you want work that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career, this is it. For many of our roles you don’t need your RBT certification to apply. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Some roles do require an active certification, but if you’re not certified yet, we’ll help you find your path to getting there.Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. We hire certified RBTs and motivated people ready to become one. Either way, you’ll work alongside a dedicated BCBA who mentors you from day one, not a manager, not a corporate supervisor. Two ways to joinAlready an RBTActive RBT certificationStart working and earning right awayWork with clients in your regionA path toward BCBA if you want itNot certified yetA clear path to becoming an RBT, with a BCBA mentor from day oneMany practices in our network reimburse RBT training and pay you during hands-on learning, and we’ll help match you with the right fitSupport as you prepare for and sit for your certification exam The jobYou’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. Every day is different. You’ll follow a personalized plan from your BCBA, implement behavior strategies, collect data, and build the consistent relationships that help kids grow. Your BCBA is closely involved and reachable, so there’s no guessing and no flying solo. What’s in it for you:$20–$27/hour, based on experience and locationDirect mentorship from a dedicated BCBA, not managers or a corporate chain of commandFull-time or part-time (some flexibility across mornings, afternoons, and evenings is needed to meet client needs; not sure if a schedule fits? Just ask, we have many)Career growth support, including a path toward BCBA certificationDepending on the practice: training reimbursement and paid hands-on learning for those earning their certification You’re a good fit if you:Genuinely enjoy working with children, especially kids who need extra patience and creativityHave an active RBT certification, or the drive to earn oneHave reliable availability across mornings, afternoons, or evenings, since our clients count on consistencyCome from education, childcare, psychology, social work, or any role where you showed up for kidsHave reliable transportation to reach client homes and schoolsCan keep up physically, getting on the floor, moving around, staying active (able to lift ~50 lbs)Are at least 18, have a high school diploma or equivalent, and can pass a background check Why Alpaca HealthWe’re not a big clinic chain. We’re a network of independent therapists who chose this work because they believe in it, and we match every RBT with a BCBA who mentors, not manages. We match families with providers who have availability now, and we work where families actually are. If you want a career where you see the results of your work every single day, this is it. Ready? Apply now.Not sure if you qualify? Apply anyway and tell us about yourself. We’d rather talk to one more curious person than miss someone great.

jobs.title: Mental Health Therapist at Transformations Care Network
jobs.description: Employer: Transformations Care Network Expires: 10/29/2026 Join us at Harmony, a member of Transformations Care Network (TCN), as we embark on an exciting journey to empower Mental Health Therapists like you to make a difference in the field of behavioral health. We are committed to improving access to mental health care in our communities which means we are committed to being a great place to be a therapist. As a Therapist on our team, you will experience an environment where both you and your clients can thrive. Emerging, early career therapists appreciate a collaborative environment, where they are supported by a clinical team that prioritizes growth and development as they work to gain licensure. Our clinics provide a supportive space to practice therapeutic interventions and develop skills that impact our diverse local community. Licensed Therapists appreciate the ability to practice in a sustainable and personalized way, with the support of a clinical and administrative team. Leadership and supervision opportunities allow our Therapists to build a career that works for them while guiding the next generation of mental health providers. Key Responsibilities Conduct culturally sensitive, strength-based assessments for new clients and families, creating a welcoming and understanding environment for diverse backgrounds. Provide tailored outpatient individual and family therapy based on the unique needs and circumstances of each client, fostering a path to healing and resilience. Develop comprehensive crisis plans, safety plans, relapse prevention plans, and wellness plans, supporting the maintenance of stable functioning and empowering clients in their mental health journey. Actively participate in case consultations, agency meetings, and discharge planning, contributing your expertise to enhance client care. Ensure timely completion of billing, documentation, individualized treatment plans, and insurance authorization forms, upholding the highest standards of professional responsibility. Engage in collaborative care with our team of psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, dietitians, administrative staff, and fellow therapists, to provide a holistic approach to mental health care. Qualifications Possess a Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Counseling, or a related field. If required, provisional license per state regulation. Educational background that leads to or has resulted in professional licensing. Passionate about mental health and committed to providing high-quality care. Dedicated to ongoing professional development in mental health including free supervision and continuing education. Eager to collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to enhance client care. Strong commitment to ethical practice and maintaining confidentiality. Excellent communication skills and ability to build rapport with clients and families. Ability to manage time effectively and complete documentation and administrative tasks efficiently. Explore the Advantages of Joining Our Team: Enjoy competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, low-cost virtual care, dependent and domestic partner coverage, 401K, and more, designed to support your well-being and financial security. Immerse yourself in a community united by a deep commitment to enhance mental health and revolutionize the care that clients receive. Embrace a journey of growth and development through continuous learning, guided by seasoned professionals, fostering your career growth in a nurturing environment. Play a pivotal role in reshaping how mental health care is perceived and delivered in your local community as well as on a national scale, with your efforts directly improving client lives. Deliver mental health care in a sustainable way, with the support and tools you need to thrive. Thrive in an environment that celebrates collaborative success, driven by effective communication, support, and unity. Receive comprehensive onboarding and ongoing educational resources, tailored to cultivate your talents, and assure your triumph in your role. Harmony is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base compensation range for this role is $33 – $53 per billable unit. Actual compensation may vary based on licensure, experience, market-driven enhancements, and incentive opportunities available for this role. These ranges represent our current standard compensation practices and may be adjusted over time to remain competitive and aligned with organizational needs. Transformations Care Network is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace.

jobs.description: Employer: Transformations Care Network Expires: 10/29/2026 Join us at Harmony, a member of Transformations Care Network (TCN), as we embark on an exciting journey to empower Mental Health Therapists like you to make a difference in the field of behavioral health. We are committed to improving access to mental health care in our communities which means we are committed to being a great place to be a therapist. As a Therapist on our team, you will experience an environment where both you and your clients can thrive. Emerging, early career therapists appreciate a collaborative environment, where they are supported by a clinical team that prioritizes growth and development as they work to gain licensure. Our clinics provide a supportive space to practice therapeutic interventions and develop skills that impact our diverse local community. Licensed Therapists appreciate the ability to practice in a sustainable and personalized way, with the support of a clinical and administrative team. Leadership and supervision opportunities allow our Therapists to build a career that works for them while guiding the next generation of mental health providers. Key Responsibilities Conduct culturally sensitive, strength-based assessments for new clients and families, creating a welcoming and understanding environment for diverse backgrounds. Provide tailored outpatient individual and family therapy based on the unique needs and circumstances of each client, fostering a path to healing and resilience. Develop comprehensive crisis plans, safety plans, relapse prevention plans, and wellness plans, supporting the maintenance of stable functioning and empowering clients in their mental health journey. Actively participate in case consultations, agency meetings, and discharge planning, contributing your expertise to enhance client care. Ensure timely completion of billing, documentation, individualized treatment plans, and insurance authorization forms, upholding the highest standards of professional responsibility. Engage in collaborative care with our team of psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, dietitians, administrative staff, and fellow therapists, to provide a holistic approach to mental health care. Qualifications Possess a Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Counseling, or a related field. If required, provisional license per state regulation. Educational background that leads to or has resulted in professional licensing. Passionate about mental health and committed to providing high-quality care. Dedicated to ongoing professional development in mental health including free supervision and continuing education. Eager to collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to enhance client care. Strong commitment to ethical practice and maintaining confidentiality. Excellent communication skills and ability to build rapport with clients and families. Ability to manage time effectively and complete documentation and administrative tasks efficiently. Explore the Advantages of Joining Our Team: Enjoy competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, low-cost virtual care, dependent and domestic partner coverage, 401K, and more, designed to support your well-being and financial security. Immerse yourself in a community united by a deep commitment to enhance mental health and revolutionize the care that clients receive. Embrace a journey of growth and development through continuous learning, guided by seasoned professionals, fostering your career growth in a nurturing environment. Play a pivotal role in reshaping how mental health care is perceived and delivered in your local community as well as on a national scale, with your efforts directly improving client lives. Deliver mental health care in a sustainable way, with the support and tools you need to thrive. Thrive in an environment that celebrates collaborative success, driven by effective communication, support, and unity. Receive comprehensive onboarding and ongoing educational resources, tailored to cultivate your talents, and assure your triumph in your role. Actual compensation may vary based on licensure, experience, market-driven enhancements, and incentive opportunities available for this role. jobs.description: Employer: Alpaca Health Expires: 10/29/2026 Alpaca HealthWork Location: In Person If you want work that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career, this is it. For many of our roles you don’t need your RBT certification to apply. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Some roles do require an active certification, but if you’re not certified yet, we’ll help you find your path to getting there.Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. Two ways to joinAlready an RBTActive RBT certificationStart working and earning right awayWork with clients in your regionA path toward BCBA if you want itNot certified yetA clear path to becoming an RBT, with a BCBA mentor from day oneMany practices in our network reimburse RBT training and pay you during hands-on learning, and we’ll help match you with the right fitSupport as you prepare for and sit for your certification exam The jobYou’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. Every day is different. You’ll follow a personalized plan from your BCBA, implement behavior strategies, collect data, and build the consistent relationships that help kids grow. Your BCBA is closely involved and reachable, so there’s no guessing and no flying solo. What’s in it for you:$20–$27/hour, based on experience and locationDirect mentorship from a dedicated BCBA, not managers or a corporate chain of commandFull-time or part-time (some flexibility across mornings, afternoons, and evenings is needed to meet client needs; not sure if a schedule fits? jobs.title: Licensed Behavioral Health Clinician / Psychotherapist - LCSW, LMHC, LMFT, Psychologist at Memory Training Centers of Florida
jobs.description: Employer: Memory Training Centers of Florida Expires: 10/29/2026 Join Memory Training Centers of Florida as a part-time independent contractor providing psychotherapy and memory-focused support to seniors within local senior living communities. We welcome Licensed Clinical Social Workers (LCSW), Licensed Mental Health Counselors (LMHC), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists (LMFT), and licensed Psychologists with a PsyD or PhD. Build a consistent schedule, expand your clinical experience, and earn additional income through rewarding work with older adults. We have ON-SITE openings in the following cities: Aventura, Cutler Bay, Coral Gables, Kendall, North Miami Beach Clinicians are paired with seniors residing in secure retirement communities located within approximately 20–25 minutes of their home or work address. Most clients will be concentrated within one or two nearby communities to minimize travel time and maximize efficiency. We understand that gas prices are high and make every effort to keep travel convenient and manageable. Memory Training Centers of Florida is a clinical practice with the mission of optimizing the quality of life for seniors in Florida. We do this through targeted interventions aimed at improving memory skills, addressing mental health needs, and developing strategies for independence. Our program is individualized for each patient and includes family, community staff, and medical professionals to ensure an effective team approach. Memory Training Centers of Florida is rapidly growing throughout Florida and has tremendous opportunities for growth! Each clinician / Psychotherapist will receive complementary training, ongoing support, multiple treatment resources, uncapped referral bonuses, and flexible scheduling. Do not miss this opportunity to be a part of a rapidly growing field, within a collaborative team, and make a meaningful difference in the lives of seniors! Part-time or Per Diem contract positions rate is $50 - 60/hr We have ON-SITE openings in the following cities: Boca Raton, Boyton Beach, Delray Beach, Lantana, Palm Beach Gardens, Wellington.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Mental Health Therapist at Transformations Care Network
jobs.description: Employer: Transformations Care Network Expires: 10/29/2026 Join us at Harmony, a member of Transformations Care Network (TCN), as we embark on an exciting journey to empower Mental Health Therapists like you to make a difference in the field of behavioral health. We are committed to improving access to mental health care in our communities which means we are committed to being a great place to be a therapist. As a Therapist on our team, you will experience an environment where both you and your clients can thrive. Emerging, early career therapists appreciate a collaborative environment, where they are supported by a clinical team that prioritizes growth and development as they work to gain licensure. Our clinics provide a supportive space to practice therapeutic interventions and develop skills that impact our diverse local community. Licensed Therapists appreciate the ability to practice in a sustainable and personalized way, with the support of a clinical and administrative team. Leadership and supervision opportunities allow our Therapists to build a career that works for them while guiding the next generation of mental health providers. Key Responsibilities Conduct culturally sensitive, strength-based assessments for new clients and families, creating a welcoming and understanding environment for diverse backgrounds. Provide tailored outpatient individual and family therapy based on the unique needs and circumstances of each client, fostering a path to healing and resilience. Develop comprehensive crisis plans, safety plans, relapse prevention plans, and wellness plans, supporting the maintenance of stable functioning and empowering clients in their mental health journey. Actively participate in case consultations, agency meetings, and discharge planning, contributing your expertise to enhance client care. Ensure timely completion of billing, documentation, individualized treatment plans, and insurance authorization forms, upholding the highest standards of professional responsibility. Engage in collaborative care with our team of psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, dietitians, administrative staff, and fellow therapists, to provide a holistic approach to mental health care. Qualifications Possess a Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Counseling, or a related field. If required, provisional license per state regulation. Educational background that leads to or has resulted in professional licensing. Passionate about mental health and committed to providing high-quality care. Dedicated to ongoing professional development in mental health including free supervision and continuing education. Eager to collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to enhance client care. Strong commitment to ethical practice and maintaining confidentiality. Excellent communication skills and ability to build rapport with clients and families. Ability to manage time effectively and complete documentation and administrative tasks efficiently. Explore the Advantages of Joining Our Team: Enjoy competitive compensation and a wide range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, low-cost virtual care, dependent and domestic partner coverage, 401K, and more, designed to support your well-being and financial security. Immerse yourself in a community united by a deep commitment to enhance mental health and revolutionize the care that clients receive. Embrace a journey of growth and development through continuous learning, guided by seasoned professionals, fostering your career growth in a nurturing environment. Play a pivotal role in reshaping how mental health care is perceived and delivered in your local community as well as on a national scale, with your efforts directly improving client lives. Deliver mental health care in a sustainable way, with the support and tools you need to thrive. Thrive in an environment that celebrates collaborative success, driven by effective communication, support, and unity. Receive comprehensive onboarding and ongoing educational resources, tailored to cultivate your talents, and assure your triumph in your role. Harmony is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The base compensation range for this role is $33 – $53 per billable unit. Actual compensation may vary based on licensure, experience, market-driven enhancements, and incentive opportunities available for this role. These ranges represent our current standard compensation practices and may be adjusted over time to remain competitive and aligned with organizational needs. Transformations Care Network is an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace.

jobs.title: Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) at Alpaca Health
jobs.description: Employer: Alpaca Health Expires: 10/29/2026 Alpaca HealthWork Location: In Person If you want work that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career, this is it. For many of our roles you don’t need your RBT certification to apply. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Some roles do require an active certification, but if you’re not certified yet, we’ll help you find your path to getting there.Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. We hire certified RBTs and motivated people ready to become one. Either way, you’ll work alongside a dedicated BCBA who mentors you from day one, not a manager, not a corporate supervisor. Two ways to joinAlready an RBTActive RBT certificationStart working and earning right awayWork with clients in your regionA path toward BCBA if you want itNot certified yetA clear path to becoming an RBT, with a BCBA mentor from day oneMany practices in our network reimburse RBT training and pay you during hands-on learning, and we’ll help match you with the right fitSupport as you prepare for and sit for your certification exam The jobYou’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. jobs.title: Dallas College BSM Associate Director at Texas Baptists
jobs.description: Employer: Texas Baptists Expires: 10/29/2026 JOB TYPE:Full-time or Part-time ABOUT TXBSMTXBSM engages college students to follow Christ and transform the world. Our ministry priorities include evangelism, missions, discipleship, church life, and leadership development. They permeate the entire structure of Texas BSM. We aim to be a bridge between students and the local church. We want to help them grow during their college years and continue to be involved in a local church. We have over 180 staff members (employed and volunteer) who serve on approximately 135 Texas campuses. ABOUT DALLAS COLLEGE BSMDallas College is the community college system for the city of Dallas, and is home to more than 130,000 students. These students come from every part of the world and many of them have never heard the Gospel before. The Dallas College BSM exists to fix that problem. We are hiring part time or full time associate directors who will be tasked with coordinating and implementing a strategy to reach their assigned Dallas College campus with the Gospel. This position is a great way to practice the foundational aspects of Christian ministry and can grow into a meaningful career. JOB SUMMARYThe Dallas College BSM Associate Director plans, leads, and executes ministry on their appointed Dallas College campus in harmony with the distinctive BSM ministry priorities of evangelism, discipleship, missions, and church life. KEY RESPONSIBILITIESEvangelism1. Implement the sharing strategy that gives every student on campus an opportunity to hear and respond to the Gospel.2. Implement a training strategy that equips students through a variety of outreach opportunities.3. One-half of the time will be spent on campus meeting new students and training students in relational evangelism.Discipleship1. Implement a leadership development strategy that includes any Dallas College student who is faithful, teachable, and available. 2. Implement the enlistment strategy for involving new students.3. Implement the Bible study strategy that involves students in meaningful study.Missions1. Implement the involvement strategy that leads students to be involved in the Texas Baptist Student Missions program (aka Go Now Missions).2. Implement the experience strategy that gives students opportunities to be involved in short-term projects as well as ongoing local mission experiences.3. Implement the international student strategy that leads students to reach out to the students on their campus who come from other countries.4. Implement the giving strategy that teaches students the discipline of giving sacrificially to missions.5. Take leadership in mission trips as required by the Dallas College BSM program.Church Life1. Implement the church strategy that leads students to be involved in a local Baptist Church.2. Consult with collegiate leadership of local churches as appropriate.3. Pursue relationships with local church staff aggressively. 4. Joining local Baptist Association(s) where appropriate for involving students in new church starts.Other Responsibilities1. Assist with working with the local leadership group effectively to provide a student ministry program that is appropriate to the campus situation and acceptable to the local Baptist churches.2. Assist with facilitating a ministry of care and encouragement to include but not limited to students, campus faculty and staff, and local church workers.3. Assist in communicating the BSM story with churches and donors.4. Attend all additional meetings and training as required to include but not limited to the following: Annual local Executive Board meetingsLocal leadership group meetingsStudent leadership meetingsWeekly programs through BSMMission TripsPersonal meetings with students for discipleship/leadership development and others deemed necessary by the Center for Collegiate Ministry and/or the local leadership groupTXBSM Annual Staff Training Retreat (always last week of July)New Worker Training (as scheduled)BGCT Annual Meeting (Nov)6. Communicate with the Center for Collegiate Ministry through required reports.7. Answer phones promptly and respond to requests for information promptly.8. Maintain compliance with BGCT’s employee policies and procedures and all state and federal laws and regulatory requirements.9. Perform other duties as required. COMPENSATIONTXBSM staff members are employees of the Baptist General Convention of Texas. This position is funded through Ministry Partner Development. This means that all of the funds needed to fund the position are raised by the employee. This includes salary, benefits (insurance, retirement, etc.), social security and a 10% training and administration fee). The exact total that the employee raises has many variables so it is not available until all the benefits choices are made. Workers are required to complete PD Bootcamp training and be fully funded before completing the hiring process and beginning work. Fully funded means funds received or pledged.Employees are eligible for a salary review every year. Salary raises will be funded through ministry partner development.Self-funded raises can be given up to $5,000/year until the new salary reaches the median level. After the median salary level, employees are eligible for up to a 3% raise each year.Compensation levels and raises will be evaluated on a variety of factors: current support raising balance, tenure, responsibility level, size and effectiveness of ministry program, ministry budget health, and local cost of living. POSITION REQUIREMENTS, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES1. In-depth understanding of a comprehensive field of knowledge, generally acquired through an earned Bachelor’s degree from an accredited seminary (Baptist Seminary preferred).2. Active membership in a church supportive of the BGCT that is also a cooperating church within the Association and is supportive of local BSM ministry during employment. Maintain a healthy personal church life, able to lead students into local church involvement, and serve the churches that provide support to the local BSM.3. Commitment to Christian principles and teachings both professionally and personally. Knowledge of and commitment to traditional Baptist distinctives, denominational structure, and church programs. 4. Relate positively, influentially, and sensitively to a broad spectrum of persons in a variety of multi-tiered relationships and settings including but not limited to students, faculty, clergy, laity, institutional staff/faculty various Baptist organizations, churches of all sizes, cultural identities and worship styles, board and council members, Texas Baptists, and beyond. 5. Ability to communicate the vision of BSM both locally and state-wide on the association and local church level. 6. Work under close supervision and clear expectations yet exercise independent thinking and initiative.7. Make effective, timely, appropriate decisions, and maintain confidentiality.8. Provide strategic and logistical planning to facilitate meetings, conferences, workshops, and retreats as required. 9. Excellent, professional written communication skills. Including the ability to report proficiently on the local BSM ministry.10. Excellent listening, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills. 11. Excellent organizational skills, and ability to multi-task and manage a variety of tasks. 12. Excellent demonstrated leadership skills necessary to appropriately influence people to achieve a desired outcome. Ability to develop strong, consistent leadership among students and assist them in discovering and exercising their spiritual gifts through serving in BSM leadership roles. Ability to effectively lead other local staff members; requires administrative skills to include but not limited to staff selection, development, motivation, scheduling, and evaluation. 13. Understanding of Scripture and theology and commitment to lifelong study and personal growth. Communicate with students through Scripture and personal experience to demonstrate how God is leading the group. Model what it means to be a spiritual leader who communicates God’s Word.14. Strong evangelistic skills. Proficiency in interpersonal and conversational skills for sharing the message of Jesus Christ at any time in an appropriate manner fitting to the person, situation, and time. Be able to lead students to share Christ on the campus through a variety of methods and in all ministry areas. 15. Recognizable word gift in speaking before a group or congregation. 16. Ability to develop each believer into a global Christian, assisting students in the discovery of how God’s Spirit leads the Church in reaching the world for Christ through Go Now Missions.17. Provide individual mentoring and lead BSM small groups to give students the opportunity for development as a disciple. 18. Possess personal spiritual discipline that models a proactive stance toward personal, spiritual, and relational health.19. Willingness to enlist ministry partners through alumni and church contacts.20. Ability to travel to various geographic locations, including travel by car and some overnight stays including weekends.21. Requires proficient working knowledge and ability to use various software including but not limited to Microsoft Office (Word, Excel), Google Suite (Gmail, Gcal, Google Drive); intermediate level skills required.22. Speak, read, and write English. Ability to speak clearly and make self-understood in face-to-face interactions and to articulate with accuracy on the phone and through email. jobs.title: Rural Outreach Therapist at High Plains Mental Health Center
jobs.description: Employer: High Plains Mental Health Center Expires: 10/29/2026 Rural Outreach Therapist: Help Shape the Future of Rural Mental Health Care APPLICATION DEADLINE: Monday, October 26th, 2026 at 7:00am CDT. Location: Northwest, Kansas [area] | Mobile Office ProvidedPay: $75,000 per year (salaried) | $3,000 SIGN-ON BONUS! [paid in installments: $1k after 90-days, $1k after six months, $1k after one year]Job Type: Full-Time | In-PersonSchedule: Monday-Friday, 8am-5pm Why You Should Apply:As a Rural Outreach Therapist at High Plains Mental Health Center, you’ll be part of a brand-new program bringing behavioral health care directly to underserved communities across our 20-county service area in Northwest Kansas. Instead of waiting for clients to come to the clinic, you’ll take care to them.You don’t have to live in Hays. If you’re licensed in Kansas and willing to travel throughout our 20-county service area, you can bring your clinical skills to communities that need them most.You’ll have a Center-operated mobile office and a Patient Navigator/Support Staff member working alongside you, giving you the tools and support to provide therapy, assessments, crisis services, and care coordination in rural communities.We are a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC), which means we’re committed to delivering high-quality, person-centered care — and that commitment extends to how we support our staff. Supervision here isn’t occasional or optional — it’s a core part of how we operate. You’ll receive regular clinical supervision, case consultation, and support from experienced supervisors who are actively involved in your professional development. APPLY TODAY! What You’ll Do:· Start your day from wherever you’re based and head out to the rural community on your schedule.· Work from a fully equipped Center-operated mobile office instead of sitting in the same clinic every day.· Meet with patients for individual, family, or group therapy and complete intake assessments or crisis services as needed.· Work alongside your Patient Navigator/Support Staff member to connect patients with resources, coordinate care, and address needs beyond the therapy session.· Collaborate with healthcare providers, hospitals, schools, community organizations, and other partners to help patients stay connected to care.· Complete your clinical documentation and follow-up between appointments.· Adjust your day based on the needs of the community and patients you’re serving.· Stay connected to your clinical team through supervision, consultation, and ongoing support—even while working out in the field.· Head home knowing you provided care to people who may otherwise have had to travel significant distances—or go without services altogether. Why Join Us?At High Plains Mental Health Center, we’re here for you — not only for the individuals and communities we serve, but for every member of our team. Our mission drives everything we do, and that includes supporting our employees with the same compassion, dedication, and care we offer our clients.When you join us, you become part of a purpose-driven organization where your work has a real impact. You’ll provide critical mental health services to those who need them most, while being part of a team that values your expertise, supports your well-being, and invests in your professional growth through continuous learning and career advancement opportunities. What We Offer:-Competitive Pay- $75,000 per year | $3,000 sign-on bonus-Comprehensive Benefits Package:o Excellent Health, Dental, & Vision Insuranceo Life Insuranceo Paid Time Off & Extended Illness Timeo 403(b) Plano KPERS Retirement Plano Supplemental Benefitso HSA & FSAo 7 Paid Holidayso (optional) $200 Saturday OP clinic bonuso Incentive payo Convention Leave & Funds [to obtain CEUs]o License Renewalo Scholarship, work-study, & internship opportunities for employeeso $3,000 Sign-On Bonuso And more! Qualifications:· A Master’s or Doctoral degree with a Kansas BSRB license as a:o Licensed Psychologisto Licensed Master Level Psychologisto Licensed Clinical Psychotherapisto Licensed Master Social Worker (clinical track)o Licensed Specialist Clinical Social Workero Licensed Professional Counseloro Licensed Clinical Professional Counseloro Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist· Must be willing to obtain and maintain any licensure or certification required by KDADS or BSRB to provide as-needed SUD services.· Competency in using technology (computers, software, telephones, etc.)· Must demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement and apply technology effectively. Submitting Your Application:If you’re ready to take the next step in your career and make a difference in the future of mental health services, we want to hear from you! APPLY TODAY using this link: [HPMHC CAREERS!]If you have any questions or need help with documentation, please feel free to contact CAREERS@HPMH.COM. High Plains Mental Health Center – We’re Here For You!

jobs.title: Physical Education Teacher at Lawrence Hall
jobs.description: Employer: Lawrence Hall Expires: 10/29/2026 Who We AreLawrence Hall is a Chicago-based nonprofit social services agency that provides therapeutic, wellness, and skill development services to youth, families, and communities impacted by trauma.Lawrence Hall is committed to helping young people build resilience, strengthen connections, and achieve long-term success through trauma-informed, community-based support.Lawrence Hall fosters a culture built upon the principles of the CARE model and the core values of Respect, Empowerment, Safety, and Teamwork. Together, these principles are embedded throughout our trauma-informed philosophy and guide how we serve youth and families, support one another as colleagues, and partner with our community.About the RoleThe Physical Education Teacher provides safe, structured, and engaging physical education instruction to students in grades K-12 within a therapeutic day school environment. This role supports students' physical, social-emotional, behavioral, and developmental growth through standards-aligned, adaptive, and trauma-informed programming. This is a great opportunity for someone who is passionate about student wellness and enjoys creating inclusive learning environments where youth can build confidence, teamwork, and lifelong healthy habits.What You'll DoDevelop and deliver standards-aligned physical education curriculum for students in grades K-12.Adapt lessons, activities, and equipment to support students' individual abilities, IEP goals, sensory needs, and behavioral considerations.Foster a safe, structured, and trauma-informed learning environment that promotes sportsmanship, teamwork, self-regulation, and positive peer interactions.Assess student participation and skill development, maintain accurate records, and contribute to IEP progress reporting.Collaborate with educators, clinicians, social workers, administrators, and families to support student success.Support schoolwide wellness initiatives, recreational activities, field days, extracurricular programming, and assigned events while ensuring student safety during all activities.Who We're Looking ForRequiredBachelor's degree in Physical Education, Kinesiology, Exercise Science, Education, or a related field.Valid Illinois Professional Educator License (PEL) with an appropriate Physical Education endorsement or eligibility to obtain licensure.Knowledge of instructional planning, classroom management, student assessment, and physical activity safety practices.Ability to actively supervise students and meet the physical requirements of the position.Strong written and verbal communication skills.Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team environment.Successful completion of all required background checks and employment clearances.PreferredExperience teaching in a therapeutic day school, special education program, alternative school, residential setting, or similar environment.Experience working with youth impacted by trauma, emotional disabilities, autism spectrum disorders, developmental differences, or behavioral challenges.Experience implementing IEP accommodations and adapted physical education strategies.Certification or training in Therapeutic Crisis Intervention (TCI), CPR, First Aid, or similar safety practices.Experience teaching elementary, middle, and high school students.Commitment to culturally responsive, equitable, and trauma-informed educational practices.Position Requirements & Work EnvironmentWork Location: Lawrence Hall Therapeutic Day School; fully onsite.Schedule: Full-time position with occasional attendance at meetings, professional development activities, school events, or assigned programs outside regular instructional hours.Physical Requirements: Must be able to stand, walk, actively supervise students, demonstrate physical activities, and move athletic equipment throughout the school day.Work Environment: Therapeutic school setting serving students with emotional, behavioral, and developmental challenges. Responsibilities include facilitating indoor and outdoor activities and responding to student safety concerns.Other Position Requirements: Successful completion of all required background checks and employment clearances.Compensation and BenefitsSalary: $50,000 - $55,000 per year. Compensation is based on a set salary rate plus additional compensation for education and experienceAverage of 17-25 days PTO + 9 holidays.Medical insurance (HMO and PPO options).Dental insurance (HMO and PPO options).Vision insurance.401(k) with up to 5% employer match and auto-vesting.Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA).Pre-tax commuter benefits.Employer-paid life insurance, disability coverage, and Employee Assistance Program.Wellness reimbursement program.Employee referral bonus up to $1,500.Public Service Loan Forgiveness eligibility.How to ApplySubmit your resume here. We look forward to learning more about you.Frequently cited statistics show that women and underrepresented groups apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the necessary skills and abilities. Lawrence Hall encourages you to apply even if you do not have experience in all areas of essential functions.This position meets the FLSA requirements for Non-Exempt.Equal Opportunity Employer M/F/D/V.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Electrical Engineering Tutor at The Pierce Institute for Academic Excellence, LLC
jobs.description: Employer: The Pierce Institute for Academic Excellence, LLC Expires: 10/29/2026 Tutor of Electrical Engineering SkillsThe Pierce Institute | Fort Worth, TXPart-Time | In Person | $30/hourThe Pierce Institute is seeking a hands-on, technically skilled instructor to work one-on-one with students interested in electrical engineering, robotics, electronics, coding, and physical computing.This is not a traditional academic tutoring position. We are looking for someone who enjoys building things, experimenting, troubleshooting, and helping young students discover what they can make technology actually do.Our students have especially enjoyed project-based work using technologies such as Arduino, BirdBrain, Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA Jetson, robotics components, sensors, motors, LEDs, breadboards, and similar maker/electronics platforms.What You'll DoYou'll work individually with students, primarily upper-elementary and middle-school age, on hands-on engineering projects. Depending on your skills and the student's interests, sessions might include:Building and modifying Arduino or other microcontroller projectsWorking with sensors, motors, servos, LEDs, circuits, and electronic componentsCreating simple robots or machinesUsing Python to control hardware or produce a desired movement or behaviorTroubleshooting circuits, code, and mechanical systemsHelping students understand why their projects work, rather than simply assembling something from instructionsFinding, adapting, and experimenting with existing code and online technical resourcesEncouraging students to design, test, fail, revise, and try againYou do not need to be an expert Python programmer. You should, however, understand basic Python and be comfortable finding and modifying existing code so that hardware does what you want it to do.Who We're Looking ForA degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or a related field is preferred, but practical skill matters more to us than credentials.You may be a great fit if you are:An electrical or computer engineerAn engineering or computer science college studentAn experienced robotics or electronics hobbyistA maker who regularly works with Arduino, Raspberry Pi, BirdBrain, NVIDIA Jetson, or similar platformsA technically advanced high-school student with substantial hands-on electronics/robotics experience and the maturity to teach younger studentsSomeone with professional technical experience who would enjoy mentoring the next generation of engineersYou should have a working understanding of basic electronics and electrical engineering concepts and be comfortable troubleshooting projects when something inevitably refuses to cooperate.Just as important, you must be able to communicate technical ideas to children. Our students don't need lectures. They need someone patient, curious, encouraging, and capable of turning engineering concepts into projects they can see, touch, test, and understand.ScheduleThis position will begin with a small number of one-on-one students, likely up to approximately 3 hours per week.Availability on Saturdays from 3:00-4:00 PM is required.Additional hours may become available as we match the instructor with other students and expand our engineering programming. Candidates should apply expecting only a few hours initially, with the possibility of growth.LocationAll instruction takes place in person at The Pierce Institute in Fort Worth, Texas.Candidates must be local to the Fort Worth area. This is not a remote position.Part of the value of our engineering program is giving young students the opportunity to build relationships with knowledgeable people who actually work, study, build, and experiment in technical fields.Compensation$30 per hourAbout The Pierce InstituteThe Pierce Institute provides individualized academic instruction and hands-on STEM and engineering experiences for K-12 students. Our goal is not simply to help students complete assignments. We want them to develop the curiosity, technical confidence, problem-solving skills, and real-world experience that can eventually lead them into engineering and other STEM fields.If you're the kind of person who sees an Arduino, a box of sensors, some motors, and a curious kid and immediately starts thinking, “What could we build with this?”, we'd like to hear from you.To ApplyPlease tell us briefly about your experience with electronics, robotics, electrical engineering, or physical computing. Specific projects are welcome. Tell us what you've built, what platforms you've used, and any experience you have working with children or explaining technical concepts to beginners.Formal teaching experience is welcome but not required.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Aftercare Teacher Assistant at Joliet Montessori School
jobs.description: Employer: Joliet Montessori School Expires: 10/29/2026 OverviewJoin our vibrant educational team as an Aftercare Teacher Assistant, where your enthusiasm and dedication will make a lasting impact on children ages 3-12. In this role, you will support classroom activities, supervise children during after-school hours, and help create a safe, engaging environment that promotes growth and development. Your energy and compassion will help foster a positive atmosphere where children feel valued and supported. This position runs M-F from 3:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m., not including holidays or school breaks. This is a permanent position during the school year (August-May). We will fill this position as soon as possible.ResponsibilitiesMonitor students during indoor and outdoor play, snack times, transitions, and dismissal. Ensure all safety rules are followed and administer first aid, as needed.Assist with check-in and check-out of students, making sure parents sign their child out during pickup.Help organize and lead activities.Prepare, serve, and clean up after daily snacks. jobs.title: Vocational Coordinator at The Connection Co.
jobs.description: Employer: The Connection Co. Expires: 10/29/2026 The Connection Co. provides disability employment services that connect people to meaningful jobs while supporting employers and communities to build inclusive, successful workplaces. We value compassion, community, commitment, culture, and connection.TCC is seeking a leader with a passion for working with and empowering people with disabilities in their own community: Northern Wood County. We are committed to growing our TCC team through finding leaders who embody our mission and who live out our values. Ideal Candidates:- Display excellent, professional, and timely verbal and written communication skills- Demonstrate exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage a caseload productively while also leading a team- Uphold strict professional boundaries and a healthy work/life balance- Strong time management skills and a desire to work at a fast pace and in an ever-changing role- Must possess strong interpersonal and leadership skills; ideal candidates will have the ability to work as a contributing member of a team, collaborate and communicate frequently and will lead with a servant leader mindset- Demonstrate open-mindedness, adapt plans and support as needed according to what is best for each consumer and what is best for each member of the team- Excellent networking skills to grow and develop relationships with employers in the community- Unreservedly believe in, display, and encourage disability awareness, acceptance, and inclusion Summary of Responsibilities:A TCC Vocational Coordinator (VC) will maintain the role of an Employment Specialist (ES) while also leading a team of Employment Specialists and Job Coaches for an individual county (or part of a county, depending on the location) and will also work to build and develop an excellent reputation and relationships in their individual county. VC Caseload ExpectationsAs the Vocational Coordinator, you will maintain a part time caseload of DVR consumers while also leading a small TCC team. This entails:- Provide weekly employment support to youth and adults with disabilities which includes helping them prepare for, obtain, and maintain employment in your county.- Assist consumers with the following: career exploration and preparation, developing resumes/cover letters/reference lists, searching/applying for employment opportunities, preparing for and improving in their interviewing skills, communicating with potential employers, and understanding employer expectations and how to exceed them- Establish relationships with local employers and school districts to help facilitate meaningful connections between people with disabilities and employment opportunities- Coordinate job shadows and internship opportunities- Understand, explain, and implement disability disclosure and accommodations to consumers and employers- Outreach and advocate on behalf of consumers to potential employers- Keep accurate and timely documentation of consumer interactions- Maintain and submit monthly reports for each consumer on caseload- Provide job coaching to consumers at their place of employment as needed Education/Experience- High School Diploma or equivalent, required- 3 years of leadership experience, required- 5 years of employment or volunteer experience working with or supporting people with disabilities, preferred- Bachelor’s degree related to human services, special education, or rehabilitation, preferred Physical Requirements- Valid driver’s license, good driving record/insured vehicle for daily use, required- Access to a cell phone and ability to communicate via phone, text, and email in an efficient and professional manner- Access to reliable internet- Ability to model, demonstrate, and train various job duties and tasks to clients in various employment locations- Ability to meet clients at school, at their place of employment, the library, or other public places as appropriate Benefits- Flexible schedule that promotes a work/life balance- Professional development encouragement and assistance- Flexible vacation scheduling- Company provided computer/device- Salaried position with bonus and advancement opportunities- Retirement plan with a 3% company match Scheduling- 40 hours/week- This position is year round- Typical hours are Monday-Friday between 8am-5pm, with occasional weekends and evenings For more information, please contact Andrea Marty, co-founder of The Connection Co., LLC.Andrea Martyandrea@tccworks.net715-937-2884

jobs.description: Employer: Altus Schools Expires: 10/29/2026 Altus Schools are nonprofit, state-funded public charter schools serving students in grades 7-12. jobs.title: Peer Support Specialist at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services
jobs.description: Employer: Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services Expires: 10/29/2026 Peer Support Specialist (Sepulveda Adult Services) This is a part-time hybrid position based in Culver City, CA. You have the option to elect into a 9/80 flex work schedule.The pay range for this role is between $21.38 - $24.59 per hour.Ask us about loan repayment programs you may qualify for by working at Didi Hirsch.About Didi Hirsch Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services has been a national leader in whole-person mental health, crisis care, and substance use services since 1942 and is home to the nation’s first Suicide Prevention Center. We are a nonprofit organization providing care to about 290,000 people annually across our programs. Didi Hirsch has deep roots in community-based mental health and a commitment to providing culturally responsive services that are just and equitable. More than 1,000 dedicated employees and volunteers make Didi Hirsch’s work possible. SummaryAs a Peer Support Specialist, you will draw on your valuable lived experience to work alongside a multidisciplinary team, foster client engagement, provide advocacy, and connect clients with resources.
